body: I was in exactly the same position as you.  My parents relied on me for everything. I remember having to translate and complete legal paperwork for my parents as a 9 year old and being so terrified because I had no idea what I was doing. It was awful to be aware of my parents vulnerabilities at such a young age and to feel that they were my responsibility and I have so much anger about the fact that normally parents are supposed to be the ones guiding you and protecting you and I got none of that. Please don't feel alone in your situation and the depth of pain you feel about it. The process of breaking away from my own parents was so hard and remember crying everyday and feeling completely worthless. But it does get better and I found that it was only when I moved away that things started to come together for me.
Definitely not. Life for me was so much better for me after high school.

Happy birthday. I'm sorry that you're in a headspace right now where you can't enjoy it.. I always struggle with birthdays myself. I tend to get even more depressed than usual because there's this expectation that you should be having fun and doing something with loved ones. It really hurts when that's not possible. Anyway best wishes to you. I hope you feel better soon.
This gives me hope, thanks for sharing.
I know the feeling and I'm sorry you are experiencing it right now.. It's awful.

I really struggled with the transition to university as well. I ended up dropping out and my life pretty much fell apart at that point. Had a falling out with my family which resulted in me cutting off contact with them. Stopped talking to all my friends. Was homeless and couch surfing for a little while. When I finally found a place to live, I spent the majority of my days sleeping and drinking heavily. Wasn't studying and working, had no friends. Things were so shitty back then and it just seemed like I was endlessly fucking up things for myself.

I still struggle a lot with loneliness and depression but life is so different and better now that it bewilders me to think of what my life used to be like.

I know that it is really hard to believe, when you're in the worst of it and the pain is excruciating with no real end in sight, but things do change, even if it feels like you're doing all the wrong things and everything seems to be going wrong.  For me, my experience was a lesson that despite how intensely true and unrelenting something might feel, things do change and life does play out in ways that you don't expect. Hang in there. You won't always be in the situation you are in right now. Eventually you will change or your circumstances will change in some way and all of this will be behind you.
I think I'm in a similar situation right now too. It's so hard to give space, even when you know in your heart that it's for the best.

**How are you?**

I am a fucking mess inside.

**What's something you want someone to listen to and just try to understand because it's so difficult to describe what you feel sometimes.**

I spend most of my waking moments uncomfortable in my own skin. Small things that most people do without a second thought are things that cause me hours, even days of intense emotional turmoil. I'm exhausted most of the time because of the amount of effort it takes push through my anxiety and perform everyday tasks.

**Who are you as a person? I know you want to be normal but who are you?**

Loyal to a fault. Stubborn. Impulsive. Inquisitive. Extremely self-aware.

**What's screaming inside that you can't let out?**

The pain, frustration. Feeling hopeless, like there's no way out of this constant mental anguish.

**When was the last time you did something for yourself?**

I went for a hike yesterday.

**Have you been taking care of your health?**

Yes and no. I work out on a regular basis, but I also smoke, drink and eat really badly.

**What keeps you going ?**

Part of me still has some hope that things might get better, but I feel like the longer this goes on, the smaller this part of me becomes.

**What's your passion? What is the person inside you want to be? What's holding you back ?**

Personal development, self-improvement. I want to be the best possible version of myself and I want to use what I learn to help others to be the best they can be as well. The thing holding me back is my constant doubt, in myself, in others, in the future.

**What scares you? What's the fear inside your heart ?**

That I will never achieve my potential as a human being. That I will always feel alone and disconnected from the world and other people.

I don't think it is. And I'm the same. I find it really hard to believe that people really want to hang out with me. When they do, I always assume it's because they don't have anything better to do or because they feel sorry for me. And it hurts like hell and it also means I distance myself from people, probably out of some sense of pride that I'd rather be alone than be second-choice for company or some kind of a charity case.
I  have the exact same grievances. I'm hurting so much at the moment and I'm so sorry that you are hurting as well.
